name: African Alliance Insurance Plc
source: African Alliance Insurance Plc, statement of comprehensive income for the year ended 31 December 2025 (NGX filing library, Financial_NewsDocs/48053). FIGURES IN NGN, lifted from the N thousand statement and multiplied by 1000. Filed line to panel label: Revenue = Insurance Revenue; Cost of Sales = Insurance service expenses; Gross Profit = Insurance service result from insurance contracts issued, before reinsurance, so Revenue minus Cost of Sales equals Gross Profit in both years; Operating Expenses = Other expenses; Operating Profit (EBIT) = Net insurance and investment result; Net Finance Costs = Net insurance finance expenses; Profit Before Tax, Income Tax and Net Profit as filed. CORRECTION 2026-11-23: the previous version printed Operating Profit (EBIT) of minus 35.76bn and Net Finance Costs of minus 41.28bn for FY2025, neither of which is a filed line (the 41.28bn was the investment income of plus 41,278,818 negated and mislabelled). Both replaced with the filed figures. FY2023 column retained from the earlier collection except those two rows, which are blank rather than carrying a figure that ties to nothing. EPS blank because the filing prints no earnings per share line. FY2024 other operating income is not printed in this condensed statement, so PBT there is 363,001 higher than EBIT less Other expenses. Previous source string: African Alliance Insurance Plc audited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, as reported in New Telegraph (9 October 2026) and Punch. | CRON 2026-11-28: FY2025 Operating Profit (EBIT) replaced with the printed Net Insurance and Investment Result of 7,099,007 thousand, read from the statement of comprehensive income on page 3 of this filing. The value it replaced was a mis-mapped sum that omitted investment income. FY2024 and FY2023 left unchanged and flagged: that column prints two different investment income figures in the same document.
note: Both years are the issuer printed columns in its FY2024 audited statements. Insurance revenue maps to Revenue, Insurance service expenses to Cost of Sales, Insurance service results to Gross Profit, Management expenses to Operating Expenses and Net insurance finance income to Net Finance Costs, per the panel nearest label rule. Income Tax is the difference between printed Profit before taxation and printed Profit for the year and is derived, not printed. EPS is left out because the issuer's per share lines extract blank. Operating Profit (EBIT) is left blank because it cannot be reconciled to the printed Profit before taxation. Previous stored series (FY2019 to FY2015) was withdrawn on this date: its Revenue row repeated the same two values across four of its five periods and no filing could confirm the period labels; the withdrawn copy is kept at static_data/_bak_AFRINSURE_income_20261010_1353.json.

rows.derivedNote: Corrected 2026-11-28 to the filed line. The stored FY2025 value of -35,755,272 thousand was the insurance service result of -34,179,811 thousand less other expenses of 1,575,461 thousand, so it left out investment income of 41,278,818 thousand entirely. The filing prints Net Insurance and Investment Result of 7,099,007 thousand (N thousand), which is the line this label maps to, and it ties exactly: 7,099,007 less other expenses 1,575,461 equals the printed profit before tax of 5,523,546. The FY2024 and FY2023 cells are left as stored because that column contradicts itself in the same filing: the results page prints investment income of 3,197,943 thousand while the statement prints 2,932,368 thousand, and its net insurance and investment result of 4,534,180 thousand does not bridge to the printed profit before tax without an other operating income line of 363,001 thousand that the condensed statement does not show.
